subproblem.title: Bounded subsets of a k-frame span have finite H^k-measure
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let g = (g_1, …, g_k) (g : Fin k → Euclid P) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P with span G := span{g_1, …, g_k}; H^k := μHE[k]. Then every bounded set E ⊆ G (Bornology.IsBounded E) has finite H^k-measure: μHE[k] E ≠ ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (g : Fin k → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ g → ∀ E : Set (Euclid P), E ⊆ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range g) : Set (Euclid P)) → Bornology.IsBounded E → μHE[k] E ≠ ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof.

Uses frame_measure (ii), the closed-box half of Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_frame_measure: for every r > 0, H^k({t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r for all i}) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k).

1. Since E is bounded, E ⊆ closedBall(0, ρ) for some ρ ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Put r := max(ρ, 0) + 1, so that r > 0 and ρ ≤ r.
2. Let t ∈ E. Then t ∈ G, because E ⊆ G. For each i, Cauchy–Schwarz (abs_real_inner_le_norm) and ‖g_i‖ = 1 (orthonormality) give |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ ‖g_i‖·‖t‖ = ‖t‖ ≤ ρ ≤ r. Hence E ⊆ Box_r := {t : t ∈ G ∧ ∀ i, |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r}.
3. By frame_measure (ii) with this r > 0, H^k(Box_r) = ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k), which is finite (ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top).
4. By monotonicity of the measure (measure_mono), H^k(E) ≤ H^k(Box_r) < ∞, so μHE[k] E ≠ ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: E ⊆ closedBall(0, ρ). With r = max(ρ, 0) + 1 > 0, Cauchy–Schwarz and ‖g_i‖ = 1 give E ⊆ {t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r for all i}.
frame_measure (ii) gives this closed box H^k-measure ENNReal.ofReal((2r)^k) < ∞; monotonicity finishes.

subproblem.title: Translates of an integer multiplicity action depend continuously on the translation
subproblem.statement: Let P, j ∈ ℕ and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (R : IMRep univ j, with M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, H^j := μHE[j]). Let η : ℝ^P → Λ^j (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) j) be a continuous j-form with compact support. Then the function t ↦ R.action(y ↦ η(t + y)) = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(η(t + y)) dH^j(y) is continuous on ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P j : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) j) (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) j), Continuous η → HasCompactSupport η → Continuous (fun t : Euclid P => R.action (fun y => η (t + y)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the parent proof (unit orientations and dominated convergence), stated for an arbitrary continuous compactly supported j-form η in place of Φ∘ω.

Notation: μ := H^j⌞M = μHE[j].restrict R.carrier. By definition, R.action(γ) = ∫ θ(y)·ξ(y)(γ(y)) dμ(y) for every j-form γ. Put f_t(y) := θ(y)·ξ(y)(η(t + y)). The claim is that t ↦ ∫ f_t dμ is continuous.

1. (Unit orientations have norm ≤ 1.) By R.orients, μ-a.e. y has the following property (IsUnitOrientationOf): there are a subspace Q, an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_j) and a sign such that either ξ(y)(α) = α(τ) for all α ∈ Λ^j, or ξ(y)(α) = −α(τ) for all α. For such y and every α, |ξ(y)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_l ‖τ_l‖ = ‖α‖, by ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm and ‖τ_l‖ = 1 (orthonormality). Hence the operator norm satisfies ‖ξ(y)‖ ≤ 1 (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound), and |ξ(y)(β)| ≤ ‖ξ(y)‖·‖β‖ ≤ ‖β‖ for every β ∈ Λ^j. Call such y good; μ-a.e. y is good.
2. (Constants.) As η is continuous with compact support, there is C₀ with ‖η(z)‖ ≤ C₀ for all z (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support); in particular C₀ ≥ ‖η(0)‖ ≥ 0. The set tsupport η is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport η ⊆ closedBall(0, r) for some r.
3. (Measurability.) Fix t.
   - y ↦ (θ(y) : ℝ) is measurable, since θ is measurable and ℕ → ℝ is measurable.
   - ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
   - y ↦ η(t + y) is continuous.
   - The evaluation map (L, β) ↦ L(β), from MultiVector P j × Λ^j to ℝ, is continuous.
   So y ↦ ξ(y)(η(t + y)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous function of the a.e. strongly measurable pair (ξ(y), η(t + y)). Hence so is the product f_t.
4. (Pointwise continuity.) For each y, t ↦ f_t(y) = θ(y)·ξ(y)(η(t + y)) is continuous: t ↦ t + y and η are continuous, and ξ(y) is a continuous linear functional.
5. (A compact window.) Fix t₀ ∈ ℝ^P and let B := closedBall(0, r + ‖t₀‖ + 1), a compact Borel set. Suppose ‖t − t₀‖ < 1 and t + y ∈ tsupport η. Then ‖t + y‖ ≤ r and ‖t‖ ≤ ‖t − t₀‖ + ‖t₀‖ < ‖t₀‖ + 1. Hence ‖y‖ = ‖(t + y) − t‖ ≤ ‖t + y‖ + ‖t‖ ≤ r + ‖t₀‖ + 1, so y ∈ B.
6. (Integrable bound.) Put b(y) := C₀·1_B(y)·θ(y). The function 1_B·θ is μ-integrable:
   - it is a.e. strongly measurable, since θ is measurable and B is Borel;
   - ∫ 1_B·θ dμ = ∫_{M∩B} θ dH^j < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult, applied to the compact set B ⊆ ℝ^P (use integrable_indicator_iff and Measure.restrict_restrict).
   Hence b is μ-integrable.
7. (Domination.) Let t ∈ ball(t₀, 1) and let y be good (step 1).
   - If t + y ∈ tsupport η, then y ∈ B by step 5, and |f_t(y)| = θ(y)·|ξ(y)(η(t + y))| ≤ θ(y)·‖ξ(y)‖·‖η(t + y)‖ ≤ θ(y)·C₀ = b(y).
   - If t + y ∉ tsupport η, then η(t + y) = 0, so f_t(y) = θ(y)·ξ(y)(0) = 0 ≤ b(y), as C₀ ≥ 0 and θ ≥ 0.
   Thus |f_t| ≤ b μ-a.e. for every t in ball(t₀, 1), which is a neighbourhood of t₀.
8. (Dominated convergence.) By steps 3, 4, 6 and 7, the dominated convergence theorem for parametric integrals (Mathlib continuousAt_of_dominated) shows that t ↦ ∫ f_t dμ = R.action(y ↦ η(t + y)) is continuous at t₀.
9. Since t₀ was arbitrary, the function is continuous on ℝ^P (continuous_iff_continuousAt). ∎
proof_key_steps: μHE[j]⌞M-a.e., the unit orientation ξ(y) = ±(β ↦ β(τ)), with τ orthonormal, has operator norm ≤ 1.
‖η‖ ≤ C₀ and tsupport η ⊆ closedBall(0, r). For each t the integrand f_t(y) = θ(y)ξ(y)(η(t + y)) is a.e. strongly measurable, and for each y it is continuous in t.
For ‖t − t₀‖ < 1 the integrand vanishes unless y ∈ B = closedBall(0, r + ‖t₀‖ + 1), and it is dominated by C₀·1_B·θ. This bound is integrable by local integrability of θ on the compact set B.
continuousAt_of_dominated gives continuity at every t₀, hence continuity.

audit.reason: The one-line type exactly matches the prose hypotheses and conclusion. The supplied proof establishes the orientation bound, integrand measurability, pointwise continuity, and an integrable compact-window majorant before applying dominated convergence. Empty support and zero degree cause no gap. The argument is complete and independent of the parent and other children.

subproblem.title: Translates along G of an action carried by G^⊥ vanish outside a compact set
subproblem.statement: Let P, j ∈ ℕ and let G be a linear subspace of ℝ^P (G : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (R : IMRep univ j) whose measure R.measure = θ·μHE[j]⌞M is concentrated on G^⊥: R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ G^⊥) = 0. Let η : ℝ^P → Λ^j (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) j) be a j-form with compact support. Then there is a compact set K ⊆ ℝ^P such that R.action(y ↦ η(t + y)) = 0 for every t ∈ G with t ∉ K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P j : ℕ) (G : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) j) (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) j), HasCompactSupport η → R.measure (Gᗮ : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ ∀ t ∈ G, t ∉ K → R.action (fun y => η (t + y)) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (vanishing off p(tsupport ω) under concentration), stated for an arbitrary compactly supported j-form η and an arbitrary subspace G.

Notation: H^j := μHE[j], M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient. By definition, R.action(γ) = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(γ(y)) dH^j(y).

1. (The compact set.) Let p := G.starProjection, the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto G. It exists because G, a subspace of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, is complete (instance HasOrthogonalProjection). It is a continuous linear map with p(t) = t for t ∈ G (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff) and p(y) = 0 for y ∈ G^⊥ (Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff). Put K := p(tsupport η). Since η has compact support, tsupport η is compact, so K is compact as a continuous image of a compact set. Fix t ∈ G with t ∉ K; we show R.action(y ↦ η(t + y)) = 0.
2. (M is H^j-almost contained in G^⊥.)
   - G^⊥ is closed (Submodule.isClosed_orthogonal), so A := ℝ^P ∖ G^⊥ is Borel.
   - By definition R.measure = (H^j⌞M).withDensity θ, so R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dH^j (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict).
   - For x ∈ M, θ(x) > 0 (R.mult_pos), so θ(x) ≥ 1 since θ is ℕ-valued.
   - Since θ is measurable, setLIntegral_mono gives H^j(M ∩ A) = ∫_{M∩A} 1 dH^j ≤ ∫_{M∩A} θ dH^j = R.measure(A) = 0.
   Consequently y ∈ G^⊥ for H^j⌞M-a.e. y: the exceptional set {y : y ∉ G^⊥} = A has (H^j⌞M)-measure H^j(A ∩ M) = 0 (ae_iff, Measure.restrict_apply').
3. (The integrand vanishes on G^⊥.) Let y ∈ G^⊥ and suppose η(t + y) ≠ 0. Then t + y ∈ support η ⊆ tsupport η, and by linearity p(t + y) = p(t) + p(y) = t + 0 = t. Hence t = p(t + y) ∈ p(tsupport η) = K, contradicting t ∉ K. So η(t + y) = 0, and the integrand is θ(y)·ξ(y)(η(t + y)) = θ(y)·ξ(y)(0) = 0.
4. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 3, the integrand y ↦ θ(y)·ξ(y)(η(t + y)) vanishes H^j⌞M-almost everywhere. So its integral R.action(y ↦ η(t + y)) is 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae). As t ∈ G ∖ K was arbitrary, K has the required property. ∎
proof_key_steps: K := G.starProjection(tsupport η) is compact, as the continuous image of a compact set.
R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ G^⊥) = ∫_{M∖G^⊥} θ dH^j ≥ H^j(M ∖ G^⊥), since θ ≥ 1 on M. So H^j⌞M-a.e. point lies in G^⊥.
For t ∈ G ∖ K and y ∈ G^⊥, η(t + y) ≠ 0 would give t = p(t + y) ∈ K. So the integrand vanishes a.e. and the action is 0.

audit.reason: The type matches the prose; continuity of η is unnecessary. Positive integer multiplicity transfers concentration to the restricted Hausdorff measure. Projecting tsupport η gives a compact set outside which the integrand vanishes almost everywhere. Independent Lean checks confirm projection-instance inference for arbitrary G and that the concentration expression measures the complement set. No circular reliance occurs.
